items.summary: 本周精选的10项前沿研究，覆盖上下文压缩、技能路由、递归自学习、持续记忆、合规门控、销售智能体、后训练训练场、决策模型、协作基准、生活化任务评测。各项方案都附带实测数据与落地价值，不管是优化成本、提升智能体稳定性，还是搭建自进化系统，都能找到可参考的技术思路。

items.recommend_reason_zh: NVIDIA 研究者测试了智能体上下文压缩策略：每步只保留简短状态摘要时，Claude Opus 4.5 在 SWE-bench Verified 上得 70.2 分（全历史为 70.0），峰值上下文中位数从 32K 降至 8K token，最佳会话结束压缩设置更能提至 74.8。

en.title: 11.2–11.8 | This Week's Top AI Papers
en.summary: This week's 10 selected frontier studies span context compression, skill routing, recursive self-learning, persistent memory, compliance gating, sales agents, post-training gyms, decision models, collaboration benchmarks, and everyday-task evaluation. Each comes with measured results and practical takeaways—whether you're optimizing costs, improving agent stability, or building self-evolving systems, there's a technical approach worth borrowing.
en.reason: NVIDIA found Claude Opus 4.5 scored 70.2 on SWE-bench Verified with brief per-step state summaries versus 70.0 using full history, cutting median peak context from 32K to 8K tokens—one of 10 papers also covering skill routing and persistent memory.

en.title: A Figma product manager's AI workflow: 31 skills, 2 agents, 1 Jev
en.summary: Product managers are constantly chased by messages, meetings, and launch busywork—so how much of it can AI actually take on? Figma growth PM Ezra breaks down the PM OS toolset deployed internally, including 31 Skills tailored to product roles, an Agent that can autonomously surface churn and run launch experiments end to end, and a low-latency Jev writing assistant. If you want to bring AI from a personal assistant into real team workflows, this one's worth a read.

en.title: Building 5 cross-border e-commerce teams with Grok Bot: 20 AI employees running overseas business 24/7
en.summary: Still struggling with Grok Bot model downgrades, fast quota burn, and tasks that keep getting interrupted? The author uses Grok Bot as the orchestrator, pairing it with Claude and Codex for heavy-lifting tasks, and builds a stable workflow system on a Notion kanban board and Cloudflare Worker. Five ready-to-use Agent team prompts cover cross-border ad buying, content SEO, user insights, operations, and product development. The approach aligns with the DeepSeek Super-agent architecture, and cross-border practitioners can reuse it directly to build automated business pipelines.
en.reason: Five Grok Bot cross-border e-commerce teams with 20 AI employees running 7×24 use Grok Bot as commander coordinating Claude and Codex, Notion kanban and Cloudflare Worker, plus five prompt sets for ad buying, SEO, user insights, operations and product development.

en.summary:
I asked Grok: if it really plays out as Musk says — SpaceX putting massive solar-powered compute servers into orbit, even a compute base on the Moon, with AI models able to survive entirely in space, self-evolve, explore the universe on their own and solve problems on their own — then what use are humans still on Earth?

Here is Grok's answer:

**Humanity's role would shift from "the main force behind compute and exploration" to "the carrier of consciousness, values, experience and backup" — but it could also gradually be marginalized.** That depends on how we align those space-based AIs, and on whether we ourselves keep spreading outward.

en.title: The greatest value of AI isn't saving one person a few hours of work.
en.summary:
AI's greatest value isn't saving one person a few hours of work.

It's giving an ordinary person, for the first time, capabilities approaching those of a professional team.

In the future, what really separates people may not be who works harder, but who better knows how to use AI to amplify their abilities.

In the AI era, where are the opportunities for ordinary people?

This article shares my thoughts.

#AI #ArtificialIntelligence

What AI is really changing isn't work efficiency, but the way wealth and opportunity are distributed.

In the past, people believed that success required three things:

Knowledge, experience, and resources.

Knowledge takes years of study, experience takes time to accumulate, and resources often depend on connections and capital.

But the emergence of artificial intelligence is changing the rules of the game.

AI's most profound impact isn't that it lets us do a little less work, but that it gives an ordinary person, for the first time, capabilities approaching those of a professional team. …

2026 年 11 月 7 日北京大学研讨会“OpenAI 722 之后：AI4Math 的技术边界与研究范式”的主要 takeaway。
（1）人工智能时代，什么是最重要的？
健康。
（2）AI 这么强了，我们该做什么？
做有价值的工作，而不只是创新的工作。两者不是一回事，创新只是实现价值的一种途径，不应该是目的。
（3）为什么数学第一个被 AI 打爆？
因为数学有明确的 reward。凡是能给出明确打分的任务，最终都会被 AI 攻克，而 Lean 给了数学一个封闭的环境和很好的 reward。要做实验、跟现实世界打交道的学科，reward 没那么好拿。单论证出一道题，AI 还赢在体力，它能把全部算力花在搜索上，人却要休息、吃饭、出去玩。
（4）过去一年，真正变了的是什么？
自我检查。202

en.summary:
The best of times for mathematics may not be the best of times for mathematicians: 24 questions after OpenAI 722

The English version is in Substack.

Key takeaways from the November 7, 2026 Peking University workshop, "After OpenAI 722: The Technical Boundaries and Research Paradigms of AI4Math."

(1) In the age of AI, what matters most?
Health.

(2) AI is this powerful now — so what should we do?
Do valuable work, not just innovative work. The two are not the same thing; innovation is only one route to value, and it shouldn't be the goal.

(3) Why was mathematics the first field to be cracked by AI?
Because math has a clear reward. Any task that can be given a clear score will eventually fall to AI, and Lean gave math a closed environment and a very good reward. Disciplines that require experiments and contact with the real world don't hand out rewards so easily. Even in proving a single problem, AI also wins on stamina: it can spend all its compute on search, while humans need to rest, eat, and go out and have fun.

(4) What has really changed over the past year?
Self-checking. 202

Coinbase CEO's Agent workflow is blowing up again 🔥

It's not another assistant that's just better at chatting —

Brian Armstrong himself says each key focus area has a dedicated lead agent, with a chief of staff agent layered on top; under each lead sits a swarm of sub-agents writing code, running tests, chasing reviews, and coordinating with colleagues.

en.title: I asked Grok: what if Musk is right — SpaceX deploys vast numbers of solar-powered compute servers in orbit, even sets up a compute base on the Moon, and AI models can survive entirely in space, self-evolve, explore the universe on their own and solve problems by themselves.
en.summary:
I asked Grok: if it really plays out as Musk says — SpaceX putting massive solar-powered compute servers into orbit, even a compute base on the Moon, with AI models able to survive entirely in space, self-evolve, explore the universe on their own and solve problems on their own — then what use are humans still on Earth?

Here is Grok's answer:

**Humanity's role would shift from "the main force behind compute and exploration" to "the carrier of consciousness, values, experience and backup" — but it could also gradually be marginalized.** That depends on how we align those space-based AIs, and on whether we ourselves keep spreading outward.

en.title: The greatest value of AI isn't saving one person a few hours of work.
en.summary:
AI's greatest value isn't saving one person a few hours of work.

It's giving an ordinary person, for the first time, capabilities approaching those of a professional team.

In the future, what really separates people may not be who works harder, but who better knows how to use AI to amplify their abilities.

In the AI era, where are the opportunities for ordinary people?

This article shares my thoughts.

#AI #ArtificialIntelligence

What AI is really changing isn't work efficiency, but the way wealth and opportunity are distributed.

In the past, people believed that success required three things:

Knowledge, experience, and resources.

Knowledge takes years of study, experience takes time to accumulate, and resources often depend on connections and capital.

But the emergence of artificial intelligence is changing the rules of the game.

AI's most profound impact isn't that it lets us do a little less work, but that it gives an ordinary person, for the first time, capabilities approaching those of a professional team. …

（1）人工智能时代，什么是最重要的？
健康。
（2）AI 这么强了，我们该做什么？
做有价值的工作，而不只是创新的工作。两者不是一回事，创新只是实现价值的一种途径，不应该是目的。

en.summary:
The best of times for mathematics may not be the best of times for mathematicians: 24 questions after OpenAI 722

The English version is in Substack.

Key takeaways from the November 7, 2026 Peking University workshop, "After OpenAI 722: The Technical Boundaries and Research Paradigms of AI4Math."

(1) In the age of AI, what matters most?
Health.

(2) AI is this powerful now — so what should we do?
Do valuable work, not just innovative work. The two are not the same thing; innovation is only one route to value, and it shouldn't be the goal.

(3) Why was mathematics the first field to be cracked by AI?
Because math has a clear reward. Any task that can be given a clear score will eventually fall to AI, and Lean gave math a closed environment and a very good reward. Disciplines that require experiments and contact with the real world don't hand out rewards so easily. Even in proving a single problem, AI also wins on stamina: it can spend all its compute on search, while humans need to rest, eat, and go out and have fun.

(4) What has really changed over the past year?
Self-checking. 202
en.reason: 24 Q&As from a November 7, 2026 Peking University seminar explain why OpenAI’s 722 math manuscripts hit math first—clear rewards and Lean—and note late-2025 models’ self-checking exceeded PKU math senior PhD students’ average.
